title: IV. Positive conclusions: eternal beatitude's earnest; life in Christ; image restoration
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 14 close before CHAPTER FIFTEEN on eternal death. (7) Diligent plus religious meditation on eternal life leads to piety plus loathing belonging toward sin — Cap. (6) The principal good belonging toward eternal life stands as union together with God. (5) Restoration belonging toward ye divine image in man begins in this life. (4) Eternal life stands as not in us plus ye world, but in Christ. (3) The earnest belonging toward eternal beatitude in this life stands as not separated out from it as a pledge. (1–2) True beatitude stands as in God alone. So far ye porismata: there follow affirmations. IV.
pass_b_english: IV. So far the porismata: there follow affirmations. (1–2) True beatitude is in God alone. (3) The earnest of eternal beatitude in this life is not separated from it as a pledge. (4) Eternal life is not in us and the world, but in Christ. (5) Restoration of the divine image in man begins in this life. (6) The principal good of eternal life is union with God. (7) Diligent and religious meditation on eternal life leads to piety and loathing of sin — Cap. 14 close before CHAPTER FIFTEEN on eternal death.
source_text: IV. Hucusque porismata: Sequuntur affirmationes. 1–2. Vera beatitudo in solo Deo. 3. Aeternae beatitudinis praemium in hac vita ab ea non separatur ut pignus. 4. Vita aeterna non in nobis & mundo, sed in Christo. 5. Imaginis divinae instauratio in homine incipit in hac vita. 6. Bonum vitae aeternae principale, unio videlicet cum Deo. 7. Diligens & religiosa vitae aeternae meditatio ad pietatem & peccati fastidium conducit — Cap. 14 close ante CAPUT DECIMUMQUINTUM de aeterna morte.
